recipes.name: Kerala Fish Curry (Mackerel)
recipes.health_benefit: This curry is rich in Omega-3 fatty acids and Vitamin D from mackerel, which may benefit cardiovascular health by potentially helping to improve HDL levels and manage triglycerides. It also supports bone density.

ingredients.item: Mackerel (or other fatty fish like Sardines/Rohu)
Tamarind paste (or 2-3 pieces of Malabar kokum)

instructions: Heat coconut oil in a clay pot or heavy-bottomed pan. Add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds; let them splutter.
Add curry leaves, ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, and sliced onion. Sauté until onions are soft.
Stir in turmeric powder, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Cook for a minute until fragrant.
Add tamarind paste (or kokum) and water, bring to a simmer.
Gently add the fish pieces and salt. Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes until fish is almost cooked.
Pour in the thick coconut milk, gently mix, and simmer for another 2-3 minutes without boiling vigorously. Serve hot with brown rice.

recipes.name: Palak Paneer
recipes.health_benefit: This dish is an excellent source of calcium from paneer for bone health, and iron from spinach which contributes to healthy hemoglobin levels. The fiber content also supports digestive wellness.
instructions: Blanch spinach leaves for 2-3 minutes, then immediately transfer to ice water. Drain and blend into a smooth purée.
Heat ghee in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), cook for 1 minute. Add chopped tomato and cook until it softens and releases oil.
Stir in turmeric powder, coriander powder, and garam masala. Cook for another minute.
Pour in the spinach purée and salt. Mix well and simmer for 5-7 minutes.
Gently add the paneer cubes and cook for 2-3 minutes. If the curry is too thick, add a little water. Serve hot with whole wheat roti.

recipes.name: Moong Dal Cheela with Vegetable Filling
recipes.health_benefit: This high-fiber and protein-rich breakfast may aid in blood sugar management by providing complex carbohydrates and promoting satiety, which can positively influence HbA1c and glucose levels.
instructions: Drain the soaked moong dal. Blend it with ginger, green chilies, and a little water to make a smooth, pourable batter. Add salt and mix well.
In a bowl, combine the chopped onion, grated carrot, bell pepper, spinach, and cilantro for the filling.
Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) over medium heat. Lightly grease with oil.
Pour a ladleful of batter onto the tawa and spread it evenly in a circular motion to form a thin cheela.
Sprinkle a generous portion of the vegetable filling over the cheela. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.
Cook until the edges turn golden brown and the cheela can be easily lifted. Flip and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes.
Fold and serve hot with mint chutney.

recipes.name: Chicken and Spinach Curry
recipes.health_benefit: This curry offers lean protein and Vitamin B12 from chicken, vital for energy and metabolism. Spinach provides iron, which is important for healthy hemoglobin levels and overall vitality.
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown. Then add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for a minute.
Stir in tomato purée, turmeric, red chili, and coriander powders. Cook until oil separates from the masala (about 5-7 minutes).
Add chicken pieces and salt. Sauté on high heat for 5 minutes until chicken changes color.
Add chopped spinach and mix well. Cover and cook on medium heat for 10-12 minutes until chicken is tender and spinach is cooked.
Add water if the curry is too dry. Stir in garam masala. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot with brown rice or whole wheat roti.

recipes.name: Oats Upma with Mixed Vegetables
recipes.health_benefit: This breakfast provides complex carbohydrates and abundant fiber, which can help stabilize blood sugar levels (beneficial for HbA1c and glucose) and promote good digestive health and sustained energy.
instructions: Dry roast the rolled oats in a pan for 2-3 minutes until lightly fragrant. Set aside.
Heat oil in the same pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves, chopped onion, grated ginger, and green chili. Sauté until onions turn translucent.
Add the chopped mixed vegetables and turmeric powder. Cook for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are slightly tender-crisp.
Pour in the water and bring it to a boil. Add salt.
Gradually add the roasted oats, stirring continuously to prevent lumps. Cover and cook on low heat for 3-5 minutes until all the water is absorbed and oats are cooked.
Turn off the heat, add lemon juice and fresh cilantro. Mix well and serve hot.

recipes.name: Andhra Style Egg Curry
recipes.health_benefit: Eggs are a fantastic source of Vitamin B12 and Vitamin D, crucial for nerve function, blood cell formation, and bone health. This protein-rich curry also supports satiety and muscle maintenance.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and curry leaves. Once they splutter, add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for a minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato purée, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Cook until the oil separates from the masala, stirring occasionally.
Add water and salt, bring the gravy to a simmer. Gently add the hard-boiled eggs.
Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing the eggs to absorb the flavors.
Stir in garam masala. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot with brown rice or whole wheat roti.

recipes.name: Hard-boiled Eggs with Sprouts Salad
recipes.health_benefit: This snack combines Vitamin B12 and D from eggs with fiber and plant-based iron from sprouts. It's excellent for providing sustained energy, supporting hemoglobin levels, and aiding digestion.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the chopped hard-boiled eggs, sprouted moong/matki, cucumber, tomato, onion, and green chili (if using).
Add lemon juice, chaat masala, and salt. Toss everything gently until well combined.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve immediately as a refreshing and nutritious snack.
